validity.researcher_notes: Existence test applied: independent open-web search for the Arabic project name (not a full-text miss on one report, since this is a 2023/2024 project, not the 2018 EGAS map cohort). Confirmed real: Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum reported GASCO's 2023 project list in a March 2024 statement that explicitly names this project — 'مشروع خطوط تغذية الفيوم الجديدة ومدينة أطسا وتدعيم الفيوم القديمة بإجمالى أطوال 40 كم' ('feeder lines for New Fayoum, the city of Atsa, and reinforcement of Old Fayoum, total length 40 km') — reported independently by youm7.com (2024-03-04) and masrawy.com (2024-03-04), both quoting the Minister/GASCO. Both describe the project as 'جاري إستكمال' (ongoing/being completed), matching GEM's Status=construction. Current sheet ref (petro-mag.org, a Nov-2025 flipbook-viewer magazine) could not be machine-verified for the construction/length values — WebFetch only surfaced the magazine's cover/table-of-contents ('أنابيب البترول' listed on p.74), and a raw curl shows the actual page content loads via JS/an internal viewer, not static HTML, so the url_verifier substring misses are a technical access limitation, not evidence the citation is wrong. gem.wiki's separate page for the sibling segment (New_Fayoum_Gas_Pipeline, P6686, read for leads only, never cited) lists further Arabic coverage of the same project (dostor.org, elfagr.org, petroleumfuture.net) that could not be independently re-verified here (elfagr 403 block; dostor 200 but page no longer contains 'أطسا' — link rot/reorg, not proof of non-existence). Net: existence + status = medium-tier confirmed (two independent outlets reporting the same ministry disclosure; not a single wire story, but both trace to one government report so I stop short of 'high').

validity.researcher_notes: Duplicate/identity check per the watchlist question 'P8011 Atsa vs P8012 Old Fayoum - both Fayoum-area; related?'. Answer: related but NOT duplicates. The single GASCO project named above ('New Fayoum + Atsa + reinforce Old Fayoum, 40 km total') maps onto exactly THREE separate GEM rows: P8011 Atsa (9.5 km), P8012 Old Fayoum (12.0 km, in this batch), and P6686 New Fayoum Gas Pipeline (18.5 km, 24in, status=construction — outside this 40-row scope, found via GEM's own tracker CSV, not gem.wiki). Sum: 9.5 + 12.0 + 18.5 = 40.0 km, matching the government's stated aggregate EXACTLY. This is strong internal corroboration that the three-way split is correct and non-overlapping (a double-count would not sum cleanly to the official total). Caveat: I cannot rule out that NA derived Atsa's 9.5 km by subtracting the other two segments' lengths from the known 40 km total rather than sourcing it directly — if so the length figure is arithmetically consistent but not independently sourced (see spec finding below). No evidence of a fourth or duplicate row for this project elsewhere in the roster.

validity.recommendation: Leave Length=9.5km/Diameter=16in as-is (no contradicting evidence found), but note in ResearcherNotes that the segment-specific figures are corroborated only by internal consistency (sum-to-total) and an inaccessible source, not by an independently readable document — worth a follow-up if a GASCO technical spec sheet or tender document for this specific line surfaces.
validity.researcher_notes: Spec check on Length (9.5 km) and Diameter (16 in) specifically. No open-web source independently states a per-segment length or diameter for the Atsa line — every source found (youm7, masrawy, and gem.wiki's citation list) reports only the THREE-SEGMENT PROJECT AGGREGATE (40 km total), never breaking out Atsa's own figure. The sheet's current ref (petro-mag.org) could not be machine-verified: url_verifier and WebFetch both show the site delivers only a magazine cover/TOC to a static fetch (JS-rendered flipbook viewer), so I could not confirm or refute the 9.5 km / 16in figures against it either way — this is a genuine access gap, not a confirmed miss, and I did not find a downloadable PDF endpoint for the issue. The only supporting arithmetic is that 9.5 km is exactly what remains of the official 40 km total after subtracting P8012 Old Fayoum (12.0 km) and P6686 New Fayoum (18.5 km) — consistent, but potentially circular if that is how the figure was originally derived rather than sourced independently. Diameter 16in has no corroboration at all beyond the unreadable current ref; other project components use 24in (New Fayoum) so a smaller 16in feeder to a smaller town (Atsa) is plausible but unconfirmed. Not elevating to a hard 'concern' because no contradicting figure exists anywhere — this is an unconfirmed-precision caveat, not a material disagreement.

summary: P8011 Atsa Gas Pipeline is real and correctly segmented (confirmed, caveats): independently corroborated as part of a documented GASCO project (New Fayoum + Atsa + Old Fayoum reinforcement, 40 km total, under construction) via youm7.com and masrawy.com (Mar 2024); NOT a duplicate of P8012/P6686 — the three GEM rows' lengths sum exactly to the official 40 km aggregate; the specific 9.5 km / 16in figures remain unconfirmed by an independently readable source (current ref is a JS-rendered flipbook the verifier cannot read) so treat as a lower-confidence spec caveat, not a contradiction.
